title: Transport expert-trace edits across assembly parent structures
hypothesis: Whole-controller edits conditioned on successful expert placement traces can repair upstream phase alignment as well as seating, removing dependence on a recoverable assembly parent.

prediction.against: Matched summary-only whole-controller edits of the same three parents
prediction.rationale: A mean gain of 0.50 across two fresh parents and the unrecoverable D-020 parent would demonstrate substantial transport beyond the previously tested parent.

code_changes: scripts/compare_generation_modes.py (--assembly-study parent-transfer; built beside R-032's code instead of a research.py subcommand)

falsified_by: An upper confidence bound below +0.50 refutes the predicted effect size; zero trace-arm success on the unrecoverable parent refutes that rescue component. An interval including zero is inconclusive; the resolving measurement is another independent parent/edit pair.

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00060, run_as_is) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is the summary-only whole-controller edit of the same parent; the metric is already trace minus summary

result.notes: Three assembly-v2 parents, all 0.00 on 5 probe cases: the D-020 structure whose grasps the expert could not recover (D-021) and two fresh gpt-6.1-sol generations (seeds 3803, 3804). Ten expert-only demonstrations (10/10). Each parent got a summary-only and an expert-trace whole-controller edit (one validity correction allowed), frozen and evaluated at declared values on cases 10-39 of pool 3802. All three trace edits score 1.00 and all three summary-only edits 0.00: +1.000 per parent, 30/0/0 each; parent-level and placement-level intervals [1.0, 1.0]. The trace effect does not depend on a recoverable parent: whole-controller edits rewrite the grasp as well as placement when shown the expert's trajectory. One shared demonstration set. 205 episodes.

verdicts.reasoning: Across three parents (the unrecoverable D-020 structure and two fresh generations), expert-trace whole-controller edits score 1.00 and summary-only edits 0.00 on 30 fresh cases each: +1.000 per parent, above the predicted +0.50, with the archived unrecoverable parent rescued too. The effect does not depend on a recoverable parent. Caveat: one demonstration set shared across parents.
verdicts.next_experiment: Integrate expert-trace editing into the pipeline as a repair step triggered by an exploration-lane plateau (R-036's design), and look for a second plateau task (R-035).

verdicts.reasoning: The named matched summary-only control was measured, and paired_success_difference was +1.00, exceeding the predicted +0.50 threshold [logs/research/assembly_parent_transport/summary.json]. Both reported parent-level and placement-level intervals were [1.00, 1.00], excluding zero [logs/research/assembly_parent_transport/summary.json]. All three trace edits achieved 1.00 success against 0.00 for their matched controls, including the archived unrecoverable parent, so the rescue component also held [logs/research/assembly_parent_transport/summary.json]. This supports transport across the tested parents; the shared demonstration set limits generalization, and endpoint success alone does not identify which controller phases changed [logs/research/assembly_parent_transport/summary.json].
